proposal.explanation: The bug was in the write_full calculation for FRAME_FIFO mode. In FRAME_FIFO mode, the speculative write pointer (wr_ptr_cur_reg) is incremented for each beat of a frame, while the committed write pointer (wr_ptr_reg) only advances at the end of a good frame. The original write_full condition used wr_ptr_reg (committed pointer) to check if the FIFO was full, which allowed the speculative pointer to overrun the read pointer because the committed pointer hadn't moved yet. The fix changes write_full for FRAME_FIFO to compare wr_ptr_cur_reg (speculative pointer) against rd_ptr_reg (read pointer), so backpressure is applied correctly when the FIFO fills up during a frame write. All other logic remains unchanged.

review.limitation: Directed simulations plus bounded two-state comparison to a historical reference; no unbounded proof or coverage of all parameters. Fixed references are excluded from model prompts.
review.scope: A four-word FRAME_FIFO with DROP_WHEN_FULL=0 must preserve eight three-byte frames and sidebands while the receiver pauses and resumes. Every frame fits individually; backpressure must prevent overwriting unread data.

simulations.property: Eight three-byte frames fit individually in a four-word frame FIFO; no loss, corruption or drop when DROP_WHEN_FULL=0 and receiver eventually drains
